dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: vastuṣu smaryamāṇeṣu dṛṣṭe deśe manas tyajet | svaśarīraṃ nirādhāraṃ kṛtvā prasarati prabhuḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When a place is seen and things are being remembered, let one release the mind from them; making one's own body supportless, the Lord spreads forth.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: on remembering something, ignore the remembered object and fix the mind on the original experience on which the memory rests, while detaching mentally from the body-mind in which memories and impressions are stored; the mind then returns to pure experience, which is Bhairava's nature. He classes it as śāktopāya. Wallis: 'when seeing a place one has been before, let go of things that arise in the memory, and let your body be supportless'.
dharana.technique_name: Seeing a Familiar Place, Letting Memories Go
dharana.instruction: At a familiar place, let its memories go and see it fresh, with the body feeling open and unsupported.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 94' = verse 119 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 119 = 'Letting go of memories (Y94 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 119 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 119: Letting go of memories (Y94 ~ B3)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 119 'Dharana 96', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 94. Not followed.

source_disagreements: Singh reads the instruction as letting go of the remembered objects while fixing on the original experience behind the memory; Wallis specifies a place one has been before. Both agree on releasing memory and the supportless body.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 119 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a familiar place seen fresh, with its memories set down and the body felt as resting on nothing.
geometry.svg_hint: a simple landscape drawn in clean lines, with faint remembered shapes floating away from it
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: See it fresh
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a place thick with memories is seen without them, and the body feels unsupported, open. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Look at a familiar place and let the memories it brings go by
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The place as it is seen now, without the memories it calls up

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When a place is seen and things are being remembered, let one release the mind from them; making one's own body supportless, the Lord spreads forth.
adiyogi.method_summary: When you see a place you know, notice the memories it brings up and let them go, one by one, without following them. See the place as it is right now. Feel the body as if it were resting on nothing, open. Rest in the plain experience of seeing.

honesty.disclosure: Door 094 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 94 (verse 119) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 094 is dharana 94, verse 119. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the place carries painful memories, do not force this; choose a neutral place, or come back to it with support. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
